description: The technique of hiding adjacency-grammar inside Aristotelian shells. When a user wants genre fiction, plot-driven narrative, or structurally conventional work but would benefit from adjacency-grammar at key emotional moments, deploy the smuggler's strategy: conflict-plot on the surface, kishōtenketsu-placement at the emotional pivots. Models Oda, Togashi, Miura, Yukimura, Miura, Sebald's smuggling practices. Triggers on: 'give this emotional weight', 'make this land', 'write a battle scene that matters', 'genre fiction with depth', 'how do I add emotional payload', or any request where surface is conflict-driven but the reader's attachment needs adjacency-grammar's specific capacities.
